title: The Daily Grind
author: John C.
desc: To look big shirtless, build in-human muscle, and boost confidence by 300%. This program focuses a lot on your abs, so if you don’t have abs at the start, you’ll have shredded abs by the end, a huge chest, wide shoulders, small legs (just joking), massive arms, and 3 steps closer to your dream aesthetic physique!

ex.note:
Flexor muscles
Take little to no rest between forearm sets. Try around 20 to 25 reps

Brachioradialis

Do 20-25 reps
Do this still with barely any rest. Congratulations, you just hit all 3 parts of the forearm!
Short head and brachialis
Short and long head
Isolating the short head, still partially hits long head

Seated on smith machine

Anterior/front and lateral/medial
Lateral/medial head of deltoid
Posterior end of deltoid
Low and narrow to domanintly hit your quadriceps

Smith Machine.
The Quadriceps, the gluteus maximus , and biceps femoris
Vastus lateralis (outer quad), vastus medialis (inner quad by your knee), vastus intermedius (middle quad) and rectus femoris (helps with hip flexion)
For these next 4, do them all without much little to no rest between sets
Lower abdominals
Obliques
Transverse abdominis
Lattisimus dorsi/lats (targets the whole lat)
The whole muscle is engaged, but mostly targeting the lower proportion of your lattissimus dorsi
Whole lat, mostly focusing on the middle though
Try not to use the machine, use the band instead. It hits the muscle better, and it’s a better simulation
Overall tricep mass builder
Lateral + medial head
Long head
Clavicular head of the pectoralis major (upper chest)
Pectoralis major as well as the anterior deltoid
High to low
For these next 4, do them all without much rest between
Lower abdominals
Obliques
Rectus abdominis (full 6 pack) and the transverse abdominis (deep core)
Very close stance, this will focus more on the vastus medialis/outer quad
Wide stance on this one. This will hit the vastus lateralis (outer quad)
This targets the semitendinosus, seminimembranosus, and biceps femoris (all three parts of the hammy)
Gastrocnemius (larger more visible muscle)
Soleus muscle (beneath the larger gastrocnemius muscle)
